newsitem.title: USA: Frontier's Rochester unit to refund $1 mln.
newsitem.headline: Frontier's Rochester unit to refund $1 mln.

text.p: Rochester Telephone Corp, a unit of Frontier Corp, must refund almost $1 million to its customers for failing to meet service quality targets for 1996, state regulators ruled on Wednesday.
The ruling was handed down by the New York State Public Service Comission, which denied Rochester Telephone's request for a waiver from service quality standards for 1996.
Those standards were established in Rochester Telephone's open market plan which took effect January 1, 1995, according to a statement by the state regulator.

The commission also ruled that, because Rochester Telephone's service quality performance continues to be below target, the company must withhold payments of quarterly dividends to its parent, until it rectifies the deficiencies.

Rochester Telephone had ample opportunity to compensate during the second half of 1996 for poor performance during the first half of the year, said commission chairman John O'Meara, in explaining the regulator's decision.
